name: Michael
source_summary: A son of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, one of several brothers given cities and gifts by their father; when their brother Jehoram succeeded to the throne, he had Michael and the other royal brothers put to death to secure his rule.
family_friendly_summary: Michael was one of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, a good king who loved God. Jehoshaphat gave Michael and his other sons gifts and cities to rule while he was alive, wanting to provide well for all of them. But when Jehoshaphat died and Michael's oldest brother Jehoram became king, Jehoram did something terrible: he killed Michael and his other brothers so that no one could threaten his hold on the throne. This sad story shows how far someone can fall when the desire for power takes over, even within a family that had once honored God.
adult_story: Michael was one of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, named among his brothers Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, and Shephatiah (2 Chronicles 21:2). Jehoshaphat, a king remembered for seeking the LORD, had given each of his sons 'many gifts, of silver, gold, and precious things, with fortified cities in Judah,' while giving the kingdom itself to his firstborn, Jehoram, as was customary (21:3). But 'when Jehoram had ascended the throne of his father and was established, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel' (21:4). Michael's death is recorded as part of this consolidation of power, one of Scripture's grim illustrations of how quickly a kingdom can turn violent even after a reign marked by faithfulness to God. The Chronicler goes on to describe Jehoram's own reign as wicked -- he 'walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he had married the daughter of Ahab' (21:6) -- and records that he died of a horrific intestinal disease, unmourned and denied burial among the kings (21:18-20), a judgment the text connects directly to his bloodshed and apostasy.
